razonamiento: The visual diagram and narration describe an architecture running on Amazon EKS with Spot instances and event-driven job management. Microservices (M.S 1, M.S. 2, M.S 3) are Kubernetes pods/jobs managed on EKS; b9 was mistakenly tagged as Amazon S3 due to 'S 3' in the label, corrected to EKS. The circle icon b10 corresponds to the AWS Node Termination Handler mentioned in the narration as managing pod draining on Spot instances (b5). Route 53, ALB, EKS, SNS, and SQS are mapped directly. The spoken flow from SNS to SQS connects the drawn EKS -> SNS and container c1 -> SQS flows.
nombre: EKS Spot Instance Microservices Architecture with Node Termination Handling

nodes.name: AWS Node Termination Handler
nodes.notes: Manages graceful termination of pods on spot instances

edges.notes: User opens Orion portal via DNS resolution
edges.respaldo: line b0->b1: https://orion / We also open up the Orion portal, and then the DNS resolution goes to the Amazon Rout of 53.
line b1->b2 / And then it resolves the DNS to the Amazon Application Load Balancer.
line b2->b7 / Amazon Load Application Load Balancer is going to send the request to our Kubernetes pods.

edges.notes: Application pod creates Kubernetes jobs for microservices
edges.respaldo: our main application running as a pod, it is going to create the number of jobs, Kubernetes jobs for each microservice.

edges.notes: Publishes event to SNS on job trigger
edges.respaldo: line b3->b4 / whenever a job gets triggered to create the microservice, it sends an event to Amazon SNS

edges.notes: SNS fans out messages to SQS
edges.respaldo: and then Amazon SNS finds out that message to SQS.
line c1->b6 / the new job that is getting replaced by this one watches out the AWS SQS

edges.notes: Handles node termination events on Spot instances
edges.respaldo: line b10->b5 / underlying it is using spot instances... for that, we are using AWS node termination handler.
